text: A bank holds your money and promises to give it back. A DeFi protocol never holds it at all — your wallet signs every transaction directly against public code. That one mechanical difference is where everything else in this course starts.

Open an account with a bank or a centralized exchange, and you're trusting a company's solvency and goodwill — FTX's users learned in 2022 that a frozen withdrawal button can erase ownership overnight. A self-custodial protocol can't freeze your wallet, because there's no account and no company in the loop.

Four properties define DeFi: non-custodial, so the protocol never takes control of your asset; permissionless, so no approval process gates who can use it; transparent, so every trade sits on a public ledger; and composable, so protocols stack like building blocks.

Trustless is the marketing word. The honest one is trust-minimized — you still trust the code has no critical bug and that no admin key can drain it. Audited protocols have still lost hundreds of millions to exploits.
Non-custodial, permissionless, transparent, composable — trust relocated, not removed. Next up: the major categories of protocols built on top of those four properties.
